newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures spent much of Friday following the movements of German bonds to end little changed and traders said they expected the contract to be range bound early next week ahead of key U.S. jobs figures.

Traders said the March bond future started strongly with Bunds and was driven higher, almost exclusively by domestic traders, to test resistance above 132.70. It failed to break through and slipped back ahead of U.S. economic data.
There was another round of short covering later in the day and the contract got a boost from a weaker-than-expected Chicago purchasing managers survey before slipping before the close.

A bond analyst at a French bank said the market looked capped around these levels and European bonds would struggle to make further gains independent of the U.S. market because of the size of the yield spreads between the two zones.
The spread between French and U.S. 10-year bonds was at 128 basis points on Friday.
He said he thought the March bond future could well slip below 132 next week.
A futures trader at a large French bank was a little more optimistic for the coming week but he also said the key U.S. non-farm payrolls release would hang over the market.
"It's a non-farm payrolls week so I fear we'll sit on the sidelines and wait for the data," he said. "My Friday call would be a range between 132.04 and 132.94-96 ahead of the numbers."
He said the price movements on Friday were largely driven by local pit traders and the proprietary desks of French brokers and that there was little interest from non-resident investors.

Analysts said besides the U.S. jobs report, seen as having policy implications ahead of the next Federal Reserve policy meeting on March 25, a German unemployment report would also be significant given the problems Germany faces in hitting the Maastricht deficit criteria.
The franc suffered slightly on Friday from the strength of the mark against the European crosses on talk of a delay to the start of European monetary union but remained in a relatively tight range.
The franc fell to 3.3762 per mark compared with 3.3730 late on Thursday.
Call money was unchanged at 3-1/8 1/4 percent.
